 Judgment

MFA.No.101434/2018 is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 17.02.2018 in MVC.No.1851/2017 passed by XI Addl. District & Sessions Judge & Addl. MACT,
Belagavi, for seeking reduction of quantum of compensation.
MFA.Crob.100138/2018 is filed by the claimants challenging the aforesaid judgment and award for seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The factum of accident, death of the deceased and coverage of insurance is not in dispute.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.

In the present case, considering the notional income of the deceased at Rs.12,000/- per month and by deducting 1/3rd of amount towards personal and living expenses, the Tribunal determined the compensation, NC: 2023:KHC-D:10503 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100138 of 2018 which needs to be modified as the parameters held by the Tribunal are not correct.
5.
The deceased was aged 24 years old and the accident was occurred on 22.04.2017.
Therefore, the notional income would be Rs.10,250/- as per the Notional Income Chart recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
As the deceased was aged 24 years, therefore, the appropriate multiplier applicable is "18".
There are four legal dependents.
Therefore, 1/4th of amount is deducted towards personal and living expenses and 40% of income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.
Therefore, the compensation under the head loss of dependency is re-assessed and quantified as follows:
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.23,24,700/- is awarded under the head loss of dependency.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10503 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100138 of 2018 6.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium, which is on the lesser side.
There are totally four legal dependants of the deceased.

Hence, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited Vs. Nanu Ram &
Others1 and National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi,2 the claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each with 10% escalation under the head of loss of consortium including loss of love and affection.

10 . The Tribunal has granted interest at the rate of 9% per annum and the same is scaled down to 6% per annum.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.17,98,000/-, but the appellants/claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.25,33,700/-.

Hence, the appellants/claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,35,700/- (Rs.25,33,700/- -
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10503 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100138 of 2018 Rs.17,98,000/-) along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Insofar as rate of interest is concerned, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is allowed in part.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. MFA.No.101434/2018 filed by the Insurance Company is allowed-in-part.
ii. MFA.Crob.100138/2018 filed by the claimants is allowed.
iii. The impugned judgment and award dated 17.02.2018 in MVC.No.1851/2017 passed by XI Addl. District & Sessions Judge & Addl. MACT, Belagavi, is modified.
iv.
The appellants/claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,35,700/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
